description: The archive windows: main, and the windows win-N that Rust opens beside it (one window per archive, as WinRAR does it). The pattern win-* matches only labels Rust itself makes (a page cannot create a window: no window permission is granted), every archive window gets exactly the commands below and nothing more, and the commands act on the calling window's own state (its archives, staged sources, extract folder, jobs and Test and Repair tool; Rust takes the window from the call, not from the page). No permission is added for multiple windows. Least privilege (AGENTS.md): the app's own commands and nothing else. The job commands (D0; pause_job pauses or resumes a running job at its next safe point, the same points where it could be cancelled, and grants nothing cancel_job does not), the browsing commands (D1), the staging commands (D2), the extract plan command (D3), the foreign-archive commands (D8: open, close, list, plan an extract; a password is sent once in the open call and kept only in Rust), the test, health, export, and repair setup commands (D4; the test and repair jobs themselves run through start_job), and the launch listener (D6: the shell's open, extract, and add verbs are handled in Rust; the webview only hears that an archive was opened or why a launch failed). The native dialogs (open, choose sources, save, choose an extract folder, choose an archive to test or repair, a copy, the new archive, a report file) are shown from Rust and dropped paths are received by Rust, so the webview never names a path: no fs, shell, http, or dialog permission is granted, and core:default is not granted. Also the passphrase and key-envelope commands (D5: unlock_archive and unlock_check_subject take a passphrase once into a zeroizing key session in Rust, cancel_unlock, list_envelopes; the create, rekey, and search jobs run through start_job). Also the update commands (T13, in-app updates: get_update_settings and set_update_settings read and change one opt-in switch, the check at start-up, which is off by default; check_for_update asks the fixed GitHub Releases endpoint, from Rust, whether a newer version exists and returns its version and release notes as text; the download and install run as the start_job kind install_update, only for the version check_for_update offered and only after the user confirms it, and the package signature is verified in Rust against the public key in tauri.conf.json before anything is installed. The webview is NOT granted any updater:* permission, makes no network request, and supplies no URL, so the CSP is unchanged.) Also open_user_guide (audit F8, Help, User guide): it takes no argument; Rust resolves the guide the installer bundles as a resource and hands it to the operating system's handler for .html, so the webview names no path and gets no fs, shell, or opener permission. The guide is static and offline. Also the simplified start screen (D10): recent_archives, open_recent, forget_recent_archives (the last archives opened; the webview sees file and folder names and opens an entry by its position, never a path), open_dropped_archive (a single .mochi file dropped on the window is held by Rust and opened on request), plan_extract_default and discard_extract_folder (extract into a new folder next to the archive, made and tidied up by Rust), and show_in_folder (Rust asks the operating system to show a folder it resolved itself). None takes or returns a path, and no fs, shell, or opener permission is granted. Also extract_wizard_setup, browse_extract_folder, plan_extract_to and plan_extract_foreign_to (Extract to..., as in WinRAR: a window with an editable destination folder, Browse..., the folders extracted into lately, and a choice to extract into a new folder named after the archive. This is the one place the webview sends folder text: the user types or chooses it, and Rust treats it as untrusted, accepting only an absolute path of bounded length with no control characters or "..", naming a folder that already exists (nothing is created from typed text except the new folder named after the archive, which is made with a no-replace create so an existing folder or file is never reused: name, name (2), ...). The restore engine then applies its own checks and never overwrites. extract_wizard_setup returns the folder used last, else the Desktop from Tauri's path resolver, and the recent folders that still exist; browse_extract_folder shows the folder dialog from Rust and returns the chosen folder text; the plans return display text and the extraction starts with start_job as for any other folder. The recent folders live in a JSON file Rust keeps in the app config folder, so the compact window's extractions are remembered too. No path, fs, shell, or dialog permission is granted.). Also foreign_search (D8: the search box over an open ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar, tar.gz or tar.zst archive; it takes a handle, the text to look for and a case flag, matches entry names already held in Rust, never file contents, and returns rows, escaped paths and folder keys, so no path crosses and it is not a new permission class). Also stage_dropped_archive (a single archive file dropped on the window is held by Rust; this takes no argument and stages that held file as an ordinary source to add, exactly as a dropped file is staged, so no path crosses either way), and open_archive, open_recent and open_dropped_archive now open a foreign archive as well as a MOCHI one, deciding by the file in Rust, with a foreign archive that needs a password answered through open_foreign_archive. Also drag_out and drag_out_foreign (dragging selected entries out of an open archive into the file manager): the webview names only the archive handle, the snapshot, and the entry keys; Rust extracts them through the same restore engine as Extract into its own freshly made, randomly named, owner-only temporary folder under the app's cache directory (refused above 8 GiB declared, deleted when the drag is cancelled, and swept when more than an hour old), and starts the operating system's drag itself, so the webview never sees a path and no fs, shell, dialog, or drag plugin permission is granted. Also set_archive_format (plan O31, owner decision 2026-10-20: the Create archive panel chooses .mochi, ZIP, tar, tar.gz or tar.zst): it takes one of five fixed words, changes which extension the staged destination takes, and returns the staged view; it touches no file and names no path, and the ZIP and tar archives themselves are written by the start_job kind export_archive, so no fs, shell, or dialog permission is added. Also MOCHI Find (find_scopes, find_choose_folders, find_remove_scope, find_start, find_cancel, find_query, find_open_hit, find_show_folder): search the file names inside every .mochi archive under some folders. Each window has its own folders and results (Rust takes the window from the call); only the name cache is shared. The folders are chosen in Rust (the native folder dialog, or the shell launch --find, which Rust validates) and the webview only sees them as text and removes one by position; the scan is a cancellable job that opens each archive read-only through mochi-core (the catalog image is hash-verified first, no file content is read) and keeps names in Rust memory; find_query returns escaped names, sizes and the scan coverage as text; find_open_hit and find_show_folder take the scan number and an archive position, never a path, and open the archive in the right window (or focus the window that has it) or its folder in the file manager. No fs, shell, or dialog permission is granted. Also the window's own title bar (release 0.9.10, owner request: one title bar instead of the operating system's bar above the app's toolbar): the archive windows are built undecorated and the page draws the app icon, the title, the toolbar and the minimize, maximize/restore and close buttons. window_minimize, window_toggle_maximize, window_close, window_start_drag and window_watch each act only on the window that called them (Tauri hands the calling window to the command; the page names no window), so a page cannot move, resize or close another window. window_close makes the same close request as the operating system's close button and Alt+F4 (CloseRequested, then Destroyed, where Rust releases the window's archives, jobs and passphrases). window_start_drag starts the operating system's move of the window from a press on the bar's empty part, and a double click there toggles maximize. window_watch returns whether the window is maximized and focused and sends each change over a channel, so the bar shows restore or maximize and dims when the window is inactive; the webview gets no event permission. These replace core:window:default and core:window:allow-start-dragging, which are not granted, and the CSP is unchanged. Also preview_extract_to and set_open_folder_when_done (owner request 2026-11-10: "Extract to..." starts at the Desktop, creates a folder that does not exist yet, and opens the folder when done). preview_extract_to takes the folder text the user is typing, whether a new folder named after the archive is wanted, and the open archive's handle, and returns what would happen as text: the folder exists or will be created, and where the files will go (numbered, name (2), when the archive's name is taken there). It is read-only: Rust validates the text as for the plans (absolute, bounded, no control characters, no ".."), only looks at the file system, and creates and writes nothing. plan_extract_to and plan_extract_foreign_to now create a folder that does not exist yet (and any missing folders above it), each with a no-replace create_dir, refusing a name that is a file, and remove the folders they made again, while empty, if the plan is closed unused; the restore engine still never overwrites. set_open_folder_when_done turns one saved boolean on or off, the same choice as the compact window's "Open the folder when done"; after an extraction that ended without an error, Rust opens the folder it chose itself in the file manager, as show_in_folder does. No path is returned that the webview did not type, and no fs, shell, opener, or dialog permission is granted. get_extract_settings and set_extract_settings (Settings, Extraction; owner request 2026-11-12) read and choose where Extract to... starts: the Desktop, the folder used last, or one folder the user chose, which crosses as folder text and is validated in Rust like the folder typed into Extract to... (absolute, bounded, no control characters, no ..); nothing is created or read on disk to answer either, and the choice is saved in the app's config folder. Also archive_info (the archive Info window, owner request 2026-11-14): it takes a handle and a snapshot number and returns that snapshot's folder and file counts, total and packed sizes and the writer's recorded chunk size and Zstandard level as numbers, and the archive file's size; it reads only the catalog Rust already holds and names no path. Also scan_setup and pick_scanner_program (Scan for viruses, owner request 2026-11-14, after WinRAR's): scan_setup returns the scanners Rust found in their fixed install locations (Microsoft Defender's MpCmdRun.exe on Windows, ClamAV's clamscan on Ubuntu) and the program and parameters used last; pick_scanner_program shows the native open dialog from Rust and returns the chosen program's path as text for the window's field. The scan itself runs as the start_job kind scan_archive: Rust checks the program text (an absolute path to an existing file, on Windows an .exe or .com, so no batch file runs through cmd.exe), extracts the snapshot through the same restore engine as Extract into its own randomly named, owner-only temporary folder under the app's cache directory (refused above 8 GiB declared; deleted after the scan, else swept), and starts the program itself without a shell, with standard input closed, replacing %f in the user's parameters with that folder's path; no archive-supplied text reaches the command line. Its output is returned as text. No fs, shell, process, or dialog permission is granted to the webview. Also find_query_many and find_choose_retrieve_folder (MOCHI Find for many names at once, spec Annex B.2.21, owner request 2026-11-17): find_query_many takes the names the user typed or pasted (at most 1,000, each at most 1,024 bytes) and three options (match case, whole name, files or folders only) and returns escaped names and the coverage exactly as find_query does; find_choose_retrieve_folder shows the native folder dialog from Rust and keeps the chosen folder as the window's extract folder, returning it as text. Retrieving the found files runs as the start_job kind retrieve_found: the webview names the scan number, archive positions and entry keys, Rust checks each against the names the scan read and that the archive file is unchanged, opens each archive read-only, and writes only through the restore engine, which never overwrites unless the user chose Replace. No fs, shell, or dialog permission is granted.
